entities.summary: Hugo Obermaier was a distinguished Spanish-German prehistorian and anthropologist who taught at various European centres of learning. Although he was born in Germany, he was later naturalized as a Spanish citizen in 1924. He is particularly associated with his work on the diffusion of mankind in Europe during the Ice Age, and in connection with north Spanish cave art, and resisted placing his science at the disposal of nationalistic and racialist interests in the Germany of the 1930s. Hugo Obermaier was a architects & engineers from Regensburg (1877-01-29, Regensburg–1946-11-12). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hugo Obermaier's work on the diffusion of mankind in Europe during the Ice Age and his research on north Spanish cave art contributed to a better understanding of human migration patterns. His resistance to nationalistic and racialist interests helped preserve scientific integrity in the face of political extremism.
